scoring_note: Editorial 0-100 estimates, not calibrated listener measurements. Contrast axes must differ by at least 20 points. Existing song scores are never overwritten.

songs.title: Respect
songs.rationale: A full-throated public demand: command, momentum and immediate payoff, rather than vulnerable private confession.

songs.title: A Change Is Gonna Come
songs.rationale: A patient, high-stakes plea that opens into collective hope; especially revealing on movement, perspective and slow transformation.

songs.title: Try a Little Tenderness
songs.rationale: Begins as a plea and builds toward volcanic gospel release; a strong test of gradual transformation versus immediate payoff.

songs.title: Let's Get It On
songs.rationale: Makes desire sound unhurried, confident and private; separates sensual assurance from longing or communal lift.

songs.title: Superstition
songs.rationale: The hook arrives instantly, but the lyric keeps danger in the pocket; dance propulsion and underlying tension can diverge.

songs.title: Tired of Being Alone
songs.rationale: A restrained but insistent first-person confession, useful against declarations that hide need behind control.

songs.title: Never Too Much
songs.rationale: An immediate communal rush with almost no menace; tests whether the groove itself can carry unguarded joy.

songs.title: Ain't Nobody
songs.rationale: A nocturnal dance-floor engine with palpable pressure, bridging sensuality and collective release.

songs.title: Sweet Love
songs.rationale: Low-pressure intimacy and luxuriant polish; separates settled affection from turbulent theatrical balladry.

songs.title: Can You Stand the Rain
songs.rationale: An elegant vocal-group promise put under stress, a useful foil to serene romance and unequivocal heartbreak.

songs.title: Back to Life (However Do You Want Me)
songs.rationale: Reclaims the dance floor without a threat; contrasts release and rhythmic assurance against harder-edged club records.

songs.title: Poison
songs.rationale: The groove is irresistible but the warning is explicit; tension and pleasure coexist rather than cancelling out.

songs.title: No Ordinary Love
songs.rationale: A slowly enveloping, meticulously produced ache that makes an intimate feeling feel ominous rather than explosive.

songs.title: End of the Road
songs.rationale: Turns a private breakup into a large public climax, separating theatrical scale from the vulnerable narrator.

songs.title: Weak
songs.rationale: Makes emotional helplessness explicit; valuable against playful control and narrative distance.

songs.title: Can We Talk
songs.rationale: An immediate, close-up request for connection, without a grand build or a performance of power.

songs.title: Creep
songs.rationale: Cloaks relational friction in a cool, mobile groove; separates emotional exposure from controlled distance.

songs.title: Waterfalls
songs.rationale: A melodic warning told through observed lives; tests witness perspective, communal reach and narrative scale.

songs.title: Brown Sugar
songs.rationale: A tactile, imperfectly polished slow burn that rewards bodily proximity more than declarative storytelling.

songs.title: On & On
songs.rationale: Loose-pocketed philosophical watching: questions arrive without either panic or a spectacular payoff.

songs.title: Say My Name
songs.rationale: Turns suspicion into rhythmic command and a public demand for clarity; the opposite of a private surrender.

songs.title: Family Affair
songs.rationale: The party is a deliberate release valve, not an invitation to brood; high movement with low lyrical danger.

songs.title: U Got It Bad
songs.rationale: Confession grows to arena-sized emotional stakes, distinguishing vulnerable absorption from romantic certainty.

songs.title: Yeah!
songs.rationale: Huge immediate kinetic party pressure: compares the dangerous edge of the club with celebratory grooving.

songs.title: We Belong Together
songs.rationale: A devastating personal loss rendered as polished dramatic escalation; intimacy and scale pull against each other.

songs.title: So Sick
songs.rationale: Small-room heartbreak trapped in repetition, a clean contrast with expansive emotional release or future-looking healing.

songs.title: Pretty Wings
songs.rationale: Lets a painful goodbye unfurl toward grace; the transformation is slow and emotionally exposed rather than triumphant.

songs.title: Sure Thing
songs.rationale: A crisp romantic proposition that remains steady in tone; separates confident devotion from fragile obsession.

songs.title: Redbone
songs.rationale: Paranoid funk that becomes larger and stranger as it unfolds; a danger-versus-release and raw-versus-polished anchor.

songs.title: Get You
songs.rationale: A slow private glow without theatrical threat; separates intimate gratitude from glossy confrontation or heartbreak.

songs.title: Focus
songs.rationale: A restrained request to be seen, drawn close rather than projected outward; urgency without bravado.

songs.title: Pink + White
songs.rationale: A cinematic reflection that turns from beauty to impermanence; strong witness perspective and evolving emotional architecture.

songs.title: Leave the Door Open
songs.rationale: Romance arranged as a fully furnished invitation, suave and communal without pressure or risk.

songs.title: Snooze
songs.rationale: Modern soft-focus devotion, direct and close-up, less an anthem than an inward promise.

songs.title: On My Mama
songs.rationale: Self-worth becomes an effortless communal strut; extremely high command but notably low danger.

songs.title: Saturn
songs.rationale: An expansive speculative escape from a troubled world; more witness and transformation than intimate certainty.

pairings.phrase: Take the room by force, or let a plea grow into history?
pairings.why: Aretha makes an immediate demand; Sam Cooke allows a slower public testimony to unfold.

pairings.phrase: Own the first second, or earn the final explosion?
pairings.why: Aretha commands at the entrance; Otis Redding builds from tenderness to a dramatic gospel surge.

pairings.phrase: Let the question ache, or turn it into conversation?
pairings.why: Sam Cooke holds historical pressure in a patient arc; Marvin Gaye moves outward through a conversational groove.

pairings.phrase: Set the whole room alight, or turn up the heat for two?
pairings.why: Otis Redding expands into a collective eruption; D'Angelo settles into a private, steady, tactile groove.

pairings.phrase: Make desire sound certain, or let the need show?
pairings.why: Marvin Gaye performs assurance; Al Green lets yearning and rougher emotional friction remain audible.

pairings.phrase: Whisper it to one person, or tell the entire dance floor?
pairings.why: Gaye stays close and leisurely; Vandross offers an immediate invitation to collective movement.

pairings.phrase: Put danger in the groove, or let pleasure have the floor?
pairings.why: Stevie Wonder threads caution through momentum; Luther Vandross keeps the same buoyancy free of threat.

pairings.phrase: A warning in the pocket, or desire under neon?
pairings.why: Wonder's brisk warning arrives upfront; Rufus and Chaka Khan turn a nocturnal mood into a larger emotional event.

pairings.phrase: Make the dance floor electric, or let it breathe?
pairings.why: Chaka Khan brings pressure to an expansive synth-funk declaration; Soul II Soul offers easy release and air.

pairings.phrase: Love that settles in, or love that has to survive weather?
pairings.why: Anita Baker gives affection a calm, intimate setting; New Edition subjects commitment to a dramatic test.

pairings.phrase: Stay in velvet, or keep the ache beneath the silk?
pairings.why: Both are polished and slow, but Sade holds significantly more danger and gradual change than Anita Baker.

pairings.phrase: Ask whether love can hold, or stage the goodbye?
pairings.why: New Edition explores durability within a vocal-group promise; Boyz II Men make heartbreak an arena-sized climax.

pairings.phrase: Dance your way clear, or dance with a warning label?
pairings.why: Soul II Soul's refined ease contrasts with Bell Biv DeVoe's spikier, more threatening new-jack swing.

pairings.phrase: Admit you're undone, or keep the secret moving?
pairings.why: SWV confesses collapse in close-up; TLC disguises conflict behind cool, controlled rhythmic distance.

pairings.phrase: Fall to pieces, or risk the first hello?
pairings.why: SWV's vulnerable surrender carries more friction; Tevin Campbell delivers a smoother direct invitation.

pairings.phrase: Ask for a chance, or demand an answer?
pairings.why: Tevin Campbell invites privately; Destiny's Child turns doubt into a communal, commanding confrontation.

pairings.phrase: Disappear into longing, or put the question on the table?
pairings.why: Sade lets ambiguity envelop the listener; Destiny's Child demands clarity with immediate rhythmic command.

pairings.phrase: Turn the breakup into a monument, or leave it at the door?
pairings.why: Boyz II Men enlarge vulnerable loss; Mary J. Blige invites a party reset with low tension and high confidence.

pairings.phrase: Warn the whole street, or question the universe from the porch?
pairings.why: TLC makes moral stakes public and vivid; Badu keeps her questions laid-back and relatively intimate.

pairings.phrase: Follow the cautionary tale, or take one night off?
pairings.why: TLC uses observed lives to build a warning; Mary J. Blige opts for immediate collective release.

pairings.phrase: Get lost in the body, or start asking bigger questions?
pairings.why: D'Angelo's intimate, raw slow burn contrasts with Badu's more distanced philosophical narration.

pairings.phrase: Dirt under the fingernails, or romance polished to a glow?
pairings.why: D'Angelo brings rough groove and assertive desire; Daniel Caesar approaches intimacy with softer restraint.

pairings.phrase: Question everything calmly, or let suspicion fill the room?
pairings.why: Badu's airy wonder stays modest in scale; Childish Gambino's paranoia turns psychedelic and ominous.

pairings.phrase: Ask for the truth with the lights on, or admit you're already lost?
pairings.why: Destiny's Child makes doubt a public accusation; Usher makes obsession a private vulnerability.

pairings.phrase: Dance to get free, or dance because trouble walked in?
pairings.why: Both are immediate club anthems, but Usher's crunk crossover carries a significantly harder edge.

pairings.phrase: Let the heartbreak take over the room, or keep it on repeat in your headphones?
pairings.why: Usher's confession builds into broad emotional drama; Ne-Yo's breakup stays close and cyclical.

pairings.phrase: The club as a powder keg, or a victory lap?
pairings.why: Both records move a crowd with command; Victoria Monét trades Usher's sharper club danger for easy self-celebration.

pairings.phrase: Make the heartbreak everybody's business, or leave it hanging in the air?
pairings.why: Mariah Carey brings loss toward collective catharsis; Maxwell lets grief unfold patiently and privately.

pairings.phrase: An epic plea, or a promise only two people need to hear?
pairings.why: Carey turns longing into a large transformation; SZA stays inside a quieter, close-up devotion.

pairings.phrase: Keep replaying the breakup, or allow a new feeling in?
pairings.why: Ne-Yo is caught in a tense cycle; Daniel Caesar offers a slower, lower-pressure intimacy.

pairings.phrase: Let the goodbye take flight, or ask for one honest look?
pairings.why: Maxwell opens a breakup into an extended release; H.E.R. holds her appeal close and unresolved.

pairings.phrase: Stand steady in love, or let love undo you?
pairings.why: Miguel makes devotion sound confident and direct; Usher admits an escalating loss of control.

pairings.phrase: Sweet certainty, or gorgeous paranoia?
pairings.why: Miguel's smooth promise is stable and low pressure; Gambino's funk is raw, untrusting and ominous.

pairings.phrase: Turn suspicion into cinema, or ask for attention close-up?
pairings.why: Gambino's unsettled funk observes danger at a distance; H.E.R. voices a refined, intimate appeal.

pairings.phrase: Love as a soft landing, or love with an edge of need?
pairings.why: Daniel Caesar's gratitude is comparatively settled; SZA's devotion keeps a sharper ache inside the calm.

pairings.phrase: Ask one person to see you, or ask the universe for another planet?
pairings.why: H.E.R. addresses one relationship in a small room; SZA contemplates an expansive escape from the world.

pairings.phrase: Hold a memory like light, or turn a warning into a chorus?
pairings.why: Frank Ocean's reflective memory is private and vulnerable; TLC projects urgent consequence toward a shared audience.

pairings.phrase: Set the whole scene for romance, or make one promise and mean it?
pairings.why: Silk Sonic's invitation is expansive and theatrical; Miguel's assurance stays compact and constant.

pairings.phrase: Roll out velvet, or strut straight through the door?
pairings.why: Silk Sonic stage romance at a measured pace; Victoria Monét supplies an immediate kinetic declaration.

pairings.phrase: Stay inside this love, or watch the years turn gold?
pairings.why: SZA's near-field devotion contrasts with Frank Ocean's expansive, changing reflection on the past.

pairings.phrase: Float toward another world, or trudge through the paranoia here?
pairings.why: SZA's refined drift contrasts with Gambino's rawer, more rhythmically insistent alarm.

pairings.phrase: Make self-worth a victory lap, or make it a demand?
pairings.why: Victoria Monét celebrates effortless confidence; Aretha Franklin applies sharper public pressure and grit.

pairings.phrase: Ask outright, or wait for them to notice?
pairings.why: Tevin Campbell puts the invitation on the table early; H.E.R. draws out her plea in a patient hush.

pairings.phrase: Electricity in the wires, or sunshine in the chorus?
pairings.why: Chaka Khan's synth-funk carries a darker pressure; Beyoncé makes communal love an open-throated celebration.

pairings.phrase: Slide into the groove, or chase the high note?
pairings.why: Luther Vandross prioritizes crisp physical propulsion; Beyoncé's chorus builds a brighter vocal showcase.

pairings.phrase: Replay the breakup, or let tomorrow enter?
pairings.why: Ne-Yo stays in private, polished heartbreak; SZA's Good Days puts more distance between singer and feeling.

pairings.phrase: Save this world, or wish yourself to a different one?
pairings.why: Marvin Gaye draws others into collective care; SZA imagines a more troubled, inward cosmic departure.

pairings.phrase: Own the whole sidewalk, or work the room with a wink?
pairings.why: Victoria Monét makes the strut maximal and communal; Blackstreet holds swagger in a cooler pocket.

pairings.phrase: Let summer turn into memory, or let romance mutate in technicolor?
pairings.why: Frank Ocean develops a panoramic meditation; OutKast's Prototype stays more compact in its strange tenderness.

pairings.phrase: Live inside the love, or narrate the one that got away?
pairings.why: Daniel Caesar offers refined gratitude in the present; Frank Ocean watches longing from a greater distance.

pairings.phrase: Make them listen, or tell them what matters?
pairings.why: Aretha Franklin's insistence is high-impact and sharp; Alicia Keys keeps moral seriousness in a gentler register.

pairings.phrase: Disappear into longing, or study it from the other side of the room?
pairings.why: Sade lets a dangerous intimacy envelop the listener; Solange steps back to observe and process the feeling.

pairings.phrase: Use the groove to hide trouble, or clear the trouble from the room?
pairings.why: TLC's smooth surface conceals relational conflict; Mary J. Blige turns the same rhythmic assurance toward immediate release.

pairings.phrase: Stay under the skin, or show your swagger in daylight?
pairings.why: D'Angelo rewards a long, raw descent into the groove; Blackstreet offers a cleaner, more immediate outward-facing statement.
